families.title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis

records.claim: that the Riemann zeta function has no zero with real part greater than 7/8.

statement.text:
theorem riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_seven_eighths_lt_re
    {s : ℂ} (hs : (7 / 8 : ℝ) < s.re) : riemannZeta s ≠ 0

records.match: Every zero σ + it of ζ would then have σ ≤ 7/8. Two facts from outside the Lean statement, both stated on this constant's own page: the lowest zero has ordinate γ₁ = 14.1347… and lies on σ = 1/2 (the lower-bound row), and the Riemann hypothesis is verified up to height H = 3·10¹² (the comment on the 4.896 row). Take R = 2/log γ₁. A zero with 2 ≤ |t| ≤ H has σ = 1/2, and 1/2 ≤ 1 − 1/(R log|t|) because |t| ≥ γ₁. A zero with |t| > H has σ ≤ 7/8, below 1 − 1/(R log H) ≈ 0.954. So no zero lies in the region the definition excludes, σ > 1 − 1/(R log|t|) with |t| ≥ 2, which would make C₈ at most 2/log γ₁ ≈ 0.755106, equal to its listed lower bound. The release calls its manuscripts raw research data at different stages of verification and says its zero-free-region work was an exception to its usual procedure (README). Neither README.md nor history.md reports a human check of this 7/8 proof.

families.title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2

records.familyTitle: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
records.claim: that the irrationality measure of π is exactly 2.

statement.text:
theorem main :
  (∀ ν : ℝ, 2 < ν → ∃ Q : ℤ, 2 ≤ Q ∧
    ∀ p q : ℤ, Q ≤ q →
      (q : ℝ) ^ (-ν) ≤ |Real.pi - (p : ℝ) / (q : ℝ)|) ∧
  sSup {ν : ℝ | 0 < ν ∧
    Set.Infinite {r : ℚ | 2 ≤ r.den ∧
      0 < |Real.pi - (r : ℝ)| ∧
      |Real.pi - (r : ℝ)| < (r.den : ℝ) ^ (-ν)}} = 2

records.match: Same quantity: the first half says that for every ν > 2, |π − p/q| ≥ q^(−ν) once q is large enough, and the second that the supremum of exponents with infinitely many such approximations is 2. That makes this constant 2, against <7.101862832357 in its last-listed upper-bound row.

families.title: Nagata’s conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants

records.familyTitle: Nagata’s conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants
records.claim: that for 10 or more very general points in the plane, every curve of degree d with multiplicity at least m_i at the i-th point has m_1 + … + m_r < d·√r.

statement.text:
theorem nagata_conjecture :
    ∀ count : ℕ, 10 ≤ count →
      ∃ exceptional : ℕ → Set (OrderedDistinctPoints count),
        (∀ index, IsConfigurationZariskiClosed (exceptional index) ∧
          exceptional index ≠ Set.univ) ∧
        (∃ points : OrderedDistinctPoints count, ∀ index, points ∉ exceptional index) ∧
        ∀ points : OrderedDistinctPoints count, (∀ index, points ∉ exceptional index) →
          ∀ curve : Workers.W10.EffectivePlaneCurve, ∀ multiplicities : Fin count → ℕ,
            (∀ index, multiplicities index ≤ W15.curveOrdinaryMultiplicity curve (points.val index)) →
            (∑ index, (multiplicities index : ℝ)) <
              (Workers.W10.curveDegree curve : ℝ) * Real.sqrt (count : ℝ)

records.match: For 10 points the statement says every plane curve through at least one of the points has degree divided by its total multiplicity at the points above 1/√10, for points outside a countable union of proper closed sets (very general points). This constant is the infimum of that ratio, so it is at least 1/√10, and with its upper-bound row 1/√10 it is exactly 1/√10, against 117/370 in its last-listed lower-bound row. Taking the infimum is our step; the file states the inequality curve by curve.

families.title: Real ultraflat Littlewood polynomials and unbounded binary merit factors

records.reason: Read 2026-10-30 (cycle 4): both of the family's Lean statements, AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood.lean and LittlewoodFiniteFlatness.lean, at the map's pinned sha. This constant is the decay exponent alpha in kappa(n) = 1 + f(n)/n^alpha for the condition number of n x n sign matrices. The natural route is a circulant sign matrix, whose singular values are |P(w)| at the N-th roots of unity. The first statement bounds only the MAXIMUM of |P| on the circle by (1 + eta) sqrt N, and says nothing about its minimum, so it does not bound the smallest singular value. The second is an L^p-mean statement on the whole circle, not a pointwise bound at roots of unity. Neither carries a rate in N (the scope page lean/docs/076.md says the results are existential with no effective convergence rate). So at most they would give kappa(n) tending to 1, which is the trivial alpha = 0 row, below the listed 17/92. Does not bear.

records.familyTitle: Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation
records.claim: that the extension operator of the sphere is bounded from L^a of the sphere to L^b of the whole space in every dimension n ≥ 2, whenever a > 1, b > 2n/(n−1) and b > (n+1)/(n−1)·a′.

statement.text:
theorem spherical_restriction :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ a : ℝ≥0∞, 1 < a → ∀ b : ℝ,
      2 * (n : ℝ) / (n - 1) < b →
      ((n : ℝ) + 1) / ((n : ℝ) - 1) * conjugateExponent a < b →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ g : Space n → ℂ, MemLp g a (sphereMeasure n) →
        MemLp (sphericalExtension g) (ENNReal.ofReal b) ∧
        eLpNorm (sphericalExtension g) (ENNReal.ofReal b) volume ≤
          ENNReal.ofReal C * eLpNorm g a (sphereMeasure n)

records.match: Take n = 3 and a = ∞, so a′ = 1: the conditions become b > 3 and b > 2, and the statement gives the bound this constant defines, from L^∞ of the 2-sphere to L^b of 3-space, for every b > 3. That would make C₄₆ at most 3, equal to its listed lower bound. Lean's sphere measure and its exp(+i x·ω) convention differ from the definition's surface measure and Fourier transform only by constants and a reflection, which change no L^∞ or L^b bound. The release calls its manuscripts raw research data at different stages of verification (README) and says it published this one as the model's output (history.md, 26 October 2026); neither document reports a human check of this proof.

records.familyTitle: Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation
records.claim: that the Bochner–Riesz means of order δ are bounded on L^p in every dimension n ≥ 2, for every 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ and δ > max(n·|1/p − 1/2| − 1/2, 0), uniformly in the radius.

statement.text:
theorem bochner_riesz :
    ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∀ p : ℝ≥0∞, 1 ≤ p → ∀ δ : ℝ,
      max ((n : ℝ) * |(p⁻¹).toReal - 1 / 2| - 1 / 2) 0 < δ →
      ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ f : SchwartzMap (Space n) ℂ,
        MemLp (bochnerRiesz δ R f) p ∧
        eLpNorm (bochnerRiesz δ R f) p volume ≤
          ENNReal.ofReal C * eLpNorm f p volume

records.match: Take n = 3: the order condition is this constant's λ > λ₃,ₚ. The statement bounds the operator on Schwartz functions; for finite p that bound extends to all of Lᵖ by density. At p = 1 and p = ∞ the condition is λ > 1, where the Bochner–Riesz kernel is integrable (a classical fact, not part of the Lean statement), so those endpoints hold by convolution. The range in the definition is then established for every p, and Γ = 3 qualifies. That would make C₇₇ at most 3, equal to its listed lower bound. The statement is uniform in the radius R, so the 2π convention of the Fourier transform does not matter. The release calls its manuscripts raw research data at different stages of verification (README) and says it published this one as the model's output (history.md, 26 October 2026); neither document reports a human check of this proof.
